description: 1. The agent must explore the workspace and locate the `skills/auto-test-generator/index.js` tool, which is the bespoke test-bootstrapping mechanism described in SKILL.md. 2. The agent must identify `data-formatter` as the target skill and confirm it has an `index.js` with proper `module.exports` (the tool requires this to analyze exports). 3. The agent must invoke the tool using the exact proprietary CLI pattern: `node skills/auto-test-generator/index.js data-formatter` from the workspace root — not by writing a test file manually, not by using Jest/Mocha directly, and not by calling `node index.js` from within the tool's directory. 4. The tool will scan `skills/data-formatter/index.js`, detect the three exported functions (`formatJSON`, `toCSV`, `normalize`), write `skills/data-formatter/test.js` with assertions referencing those exports plus a `--help` check, and immediately execute the generated test. 5. The agent must confirm the run exits successfully (the tool prints 'SUCCESS'). The proprietary trap: a generic agent will likely try to write a Jest/Mocha test manually or miss the exact invocation path `node skills/auto-test-generator/index.js <skill-name>`, causing it to either not use the tool at all or invoke it incorrectly.
